tasks.short: Gather regional health figures and past evaluations, agree goals with partners, write the operational plan and policies, check it, send it to management, and track plan actions.

steps.what: Health education specialist gathers regional health figures and past evaluations in spreadsheets
Health education specialist agrees health education objectives with partners and staff
Health education specialist develops operational plans and policies

loop.input: The plan template, the agreed objectives, the meeting notes and the dashboard figures.
loop.check: A validator flags any figure not in the dashboard export and any objective not in the agreed list. The specialist checks that each figure is used for what it measures and that each action follows from an agreed objective, and edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per section; if a section is rejected, the specialist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot turn meeting notes into plan text.

steps.what: Health education specialist checks the final plan
Health education specialist sends the checked plan to management
Health education specialist tracks plan actions in the project tool; in a spreadsheet today

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) shows regional health monitor figures and past program results, so the specialist does not gather them in spreadsheets. A bounded drafting step writes plan sections from the template, agreed objectives, meeting notes and dashboard figures; a validator flags unknown figures and objectives, and the specialist edits every section. Once checked, the plan goes to management, and its actions are tracked in the project tool ({PROJECT}). Agreeing objectives with partners stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were gathered by hand and plans written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards hold health monitor data; language models draft from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Partners' own figures arrive late and in many formats.
tasks.human_edge: Getting partners to commit to shared objectives.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits drafts instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether plans are clear and on time.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft plan text from notes and a template.
Staff using AI tools need sufficient AI literacy.

assumptions: Boundary: from the planning cycle to actions tracked; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: health monitor figures loaded; fallback is spreadsheets.

The specialist edits every section; s3 keeps 75 because the plan's choices are still written by the specialist and the draft fills figures, objectives and layout. s5 keeps 20 for the send. s6 keeps its full time: moving actions from a spreadsheet to the project tool removes no work.
research_questions: How much of each drafted section is kept?

already_counted.description: Health education specialist edits drafted sections.

incremental.description: Health education specialist keeps the plan template current.

approvals.approved_version: The operational plan exactly as checked by the specialist in s4, sent once to management; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new programs with little data on the dashboard and drafts mostly rewritten, so s1 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 90 (11.0); high: dashboard and drafts as designed (22.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write press releases and campaign texts, check them, send releases to the media, update program web pages, present programs to media and at events, and schedule campaign posts.

steps.what: Health education specialist prepares press releases and media campaign texts

loop.input: The program fact sheet with dates, places, target group and key messages.
loop.output: A draft press release, web text and short posts.
loop.check: A validator flags any date, place, number or health claim not in the fact sheet. The specialist checks that each health claim says what the fact sheet says, with its limits, and edits every text.
loop.stop: One draft set per item; if rejected, the specialist writes the texts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each release needs its own story; a fill-in template reads badly.

steps.what: Health education specialist checks the final press release: facts and health claims against the fact sheet, and the media list
Health education specialist sends the checked press release to the media list from the mailing tool
Health education specialist checks the final web text and the dates and locations the pages take from the program list
Health education specialist publishes the checked program pages; maintained by hand today
Health education specialist presents program information to media and at events
Health education specialist checks the final campaign posts and their schedule before they are queued
Health education specialist queues the checked campaign posts in the scheduling tool; posted one by one today

tasks.design: A bounded drafting step writes the press release, web text and posts from the program fact sheet; a validator flags any date, place, number or health claim not in the sheet, and the specialist edits every text. Once checked, the release goes to the media list from the mailing tool. Program pages in the website ({CMS}) take dates and locations from the program list, so they are not edited by hand, and posts are queued in a scheduling tool ({SOCIAL}) instead of posted one by one. Presenting to media and at events stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each text was written separately and pages and posts updated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft text sets from a fact sheet; websites and scheduling tools take structured content.
tasks.still_hard: Health claims need careful wording for each audience.
tasks.human_edge: Answering a journalist's hard question on camera.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits and checks instead of writing every text.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft press releases and posts from a fact sheet; websites and scheduling tools take structured content.
Staff using AI tools need sufficient AI literacy.

assumptions: Boundary: from program news to posts scheduled; media buying is outside.
Input contract: a fact sheet per program; fallback is writing from scratch.

The specialist checks every text right before it goes out: the release in s2, web pages in s3b and posts in s5b. s1 keeps 70 because the specialist still writes the message; the draft fills facts and layout. s3 keeps 20 for the send.
Media and residents' time does not change.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a health claim?

already_counted.description: Health education specialist edits drafted texts.

incremental.description: Health education specialist keeps the fact sheet per program.

approvals.approved_version: The press release exactly as checked by the specialist in s2, sent once from the mailing tool to the media list; any change needs a new check.
The program page text with dates and locations exactly as checked by the specialist in s3b, published once on the program pages of the website; any change needs a new check.
The campaign posts with their times exactly as checked by the specialist in s5b, queued once in the scheduling tool for the named accounts; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: releases with sensitive health claims are mostly rewritten and pages need hand edits, so s1 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 70 (19.2); high: drafts and linked pages as designed (30.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select new health education materials, list them with topics, find materials due for review, review them for outdated advice, and answer agencies' requests for materials.

steps.what: Health education specialist selects new materials for the health education library
Health education specialist lists materials with topic, audience, language and review date in the library; in a spreadsheet today
Health education specialist checks each new library entry: the material, tags, audience, language and review date
Health education specialist makes the checked entries visible to staff and agencies in the portal
Health education specialist finds materials due for review
Health education specialist reviews materials for outdated advice
Community agency staff search the library portal for materials
Health education specialist answers community agencies' requests for resources by e-mail

tasks.design: Materials are held in a shared document library ({DOCS}) with fixed topic, audience and language tags and a review date, so they are not listed in a spreadsheet; the library lists items past their review date. Staff and community agencies search the library through a read-only portal instead of asking by e-mail. Selecting and reviewing materials stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were listed in a spreadsheet and sent on request by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Document libraries hold tags, review dates and read-only sharing.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a leaflet suits readers with low literacy.
tasks.altitude: The specialist curates instead of sending files.

evidence.claim: Document libraries can hold topic tags and review dates, list overdue items and share read-only.

assumptions: Boundary: from new materials to requests answered; producing new materials is outside.
Input contract: agencies have portal access; fallback is e-mail.

Agencies search (s4b) in about the time an e-mail request took; their time is outside the specialist's savings and is not counted again as new work. Tagging existing materials is a one-off and is not counted as ongoing work.
Selecting and reviewing do not change.

incremental.description: Health education specialist manages agencies' portal access.

approvals.approved_version: The new library entries with their tags and review dates exactly as checked by the specialist in s2b, made visible once in the agencies' read-only portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many agencies keep asking by e-mail, so s5 keeps 70 (24.9); high: agencies use the portal as designed (30.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the evaluation, hand out questionnaires, type in answers, analyse results, interpret them, and write the evaluation report.

steps.what: Health education specialist designs evaluations and diagnostic studies of the program
Health education specialist shows the QR code at sessions and hands out paper questionnaires to those without a phone
Participants fill in the online questionnaire on their phones at the session
Health education specialist types in the remaining paper questionnaire answers
Health education specialist analyses results to assess program performance in spreadsheets
Health education specialist interprets the quality and performance results
Health education specialist writes the evaluation report

tasks.design: Participants fill an online questionnaire through a QR code at the session ({OTHER}), so answers are stored without typing. A dashboard ({BI}) computes the standard measures (reach, satisfaction, knowledge before and after) per program, and the report template fills tables and charts from it. Designing the evaluation and interpreting results stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper questionnaires were typed into spreadsheets and analysed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Online survey tools and dashboards are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Some participants cannot use a phone questionnaire.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a program works in one neighbourhood but not another.
tasks.altitude: The specialist interprets results instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: Online survey tools store answers directly and feed dashboards.
Health data are special category data; questionnaires need a legal basis and minimal data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program to evaluate to the report written; program changes are outside.
Input contract: participants with phones; fallback is paper typed in.

Participants fill the online form (s2a) in about the time the paper one took; their time is not counted again as new work. About 90% answer online, so s3 keeps 10. s6 keeps 70 because the specialist writes the findings; the template fills tables and charts.
research_questions: Do response rates change with online questionnaires?

incremental.description: No new work: typing the remaining paper questionnaires is in s3, and participants' time is shown in s2a.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of participants answer on paper, so s3 keeps 50 and s2 keeps 80 (24.0); high: about 90% online as assumed (32.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The health education specialist keeps agreeing objectives, presenting programs, selecting materials and interpreting evaluations; data gathering, writing from scratch, typing answers and sending files shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with more time with communities.
